items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section XV, List of Answers on Terminology 21:1
items.html: (To the question) What are the three vessels of the externality? In every degree there is Aba and Ima of the back and Aba and Ima of the face. For the aspect of VAK is called the back: the aspect of Nefesh is called pregnancy, the aspect of VAK of Ruach is called suckling, and the GAR of Ruach is called Mochin of VAK. And these three are called Aba and Ima of the back, or Aba and Ima of the externality. And the aspect of the NRNHY of the GAR is called Aba and Ima of the face: for pregnancy and suckling are the Nefesh and Ruach of the GAR, which are also called VAK of the greatness, and the Mochin are the GAR of the GAR. And these three Partzufim, both of the Aba and Ima of the back and of the Aba and Ima of the face, are included one in the other, for the Partzuf of pregnancy is also included of suckling and Mochin, and likewise the Partzuf of suckling is also included of pregnancy and Mochin, and likewise the Partzuf of the Mochin is also included of pregnancy and suckling. And therefore it is found that in every Partzuf there are three vessels: external, middle, and inner. The external is the vessel drawn from pregnancy, the middle is the inclusion from suckling, and the inner is the inclusion from the Mochin. And the three vessels that are in each of the three Partzufim of the externality are called the three vessels of the externality. And the three vessels that are in each of the three inner Partzufim are called the three vessels of the internality. (Item 182).
